page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. Configured with 64 physical cores, 128 dedicated vCPUs, and 4096 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, it delivers a massive 32 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware provisioning includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Accelerator hardware is absent, with zero GPUs installed.

Benchmark results highlight immense aggregate compute and memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score (85,629.49), encryption tests (110,669.62), and Geekbench ray tracing (100,661.0). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 302.32 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 122.18 GB/sec, supporting strong database metrics such as 106.84 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-threaded execution and compilation are in the upper quartile, single-core benchmarks like Geekbench (1,690.0) and stress-ng (1,893.7) place in the average tier. Furthermore, CPU-only large language model text generation on large 70B parameter models registers in the bottom quartile at 2.76 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

With its 4 TB memory footprint and attached high-speed local NVMe storage, the x2iedn.32xlarge is resource-dense and cost-efficient for heavy memory-bound enterprise deployments that would otherwise require multi-node sharding. It is exceptionally well suited for large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, real-time analytics engines, massive electronic design automation (EDA) workflows, and memory-intensive enterprise database processing.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and 64-core Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz across 128 dedicated vCPUs. Designed for memory-saturated architectures, it provides 4096 GB of DDR4 RAM—equating to 32 GB per core—alongside 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline networking, without bundled GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate superior multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, scoring 85,629.49 in PassMark CPU tests and sustaining 106.84 million Redis SET operations per second. Although single-thread throughput is average and large LLM inference is limited without hardware accelerators, the dense memory-to-core ratio offers strong qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating distributed memory workloads onto a single node. It is engineered for large-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation, enterprise data warehousing, and high-throughput real-time caching layers.
